lessons: Long‑only rules on BTC/ETH/SOL using price‑momentum and trader‑sentiment filters achieve ~2‑3% average 72‑hour returns with ~65% hit rate.
Best single‑factor tests (e.g., p_cbp+p_u_trapped_trader_exhaust) yielded 55 signals, 4.86% mean gain, zero survivors, indicating over‑fitting.
Team‑of‑two rule combos improve robustness: combined BTC/ETH/SOL strategies give mean 2.1% return, 62% hit, payoff ~1.6.
All‑coin stablecoin‑supply + Donchian channel rules produce modest 0.46% mean return, 55% hit, but many liquidations (≈10).
Validated 24‑hour low‑price, high‑supply, low fear‑greed rule yields 0.63% mean gain, 57% hit across 570 trades.
Leverage of 10× boosts average win (~5.5%) but also raises average loss (~‑3.5%) and stress scores above 1.5.
Survivor count is low: only 2–3 rules survived out‑of‑sample testing, highlighting need for continuous validation.

why.reason: Contrarian squeeze: Stablecoin inflows provide liquidity while low perp premium and low MACD histogram indicate that over-leveraged shorts and perps are underpriced relative to spot accumulation, setting up a long squeeze.

Mean reversion on extreme dislocation: Negative funding means shorts pay longs, while price at the bottom of the Bollinger band with a negative EMA gap signals that the drop has extended far beyond normal volatility and is due for a snap-back.

Smart money divergence: New stablecoin money is entering the market (top 20% supply) while price drops (bottom 20% change) and the 'crowd vs smart' divergence metric is high, suggesting institutions are accumulating the dip while retail is panicking.

Regime-aware compound: Combines a BTC-specific 'risk-on' signal (high Coinbase premium + high EMA gap + rising Fear & Greed) with a broad 'contrarian dip-buy' signal (low 24h change + falling Fear & Greed) to catch both momentum bursts and oversold rebounds.

wild.why: Gambler's Fallacy Reversal: When a coin has a long streak of hourly drops (streak < -6) AND the crowd is still heavily long (p_glob top 20%), it suggests the crowd is chasing a falling knife. The exit is a tight trail to catch the initial short-squeeze pop when the streak breaks.

Coinbase Premium Dislocation: When the Coinbase premium is extremely high (top 10%) but the 24h price change is low (bottom 20%), it indicates US buyers are aggressively paying up while the global market is stagnant. This often precedes a breakout as the premium normalizes upward.

Options Fear Gauge Contrarian: When the BTC options fear gauge (dvol) is in the bottom 10% (low implied volatility/fear) AND the Fear & Greed index is in the top 50% (euphoria), the market is complacent. guard.what: Risk guard: no second bet on the same move (correlation), total open risk capped by tail loss, daily and weekly brakes

lock.what: Profit lock: once a trade is well on its way the stop goes to break-even, and after the first target it always keeps at least half of the best open profit

trend2.what: Compass trend reader: market direction from many views that must agree (Bitcoin's 20/50/200-day trends, breadth across coins, stocks, the dollar), five states incl. sideways, smoothed so noise cannot flip it

gate.what: Trend gate: no shorts while the Compass trend reader says the market is rising. Over 7 past periods: +3.4% a month on average vs +2.0% without it, and the worst period improved from -11.9% to -2.0% a month

timestop.what: Time stop: a trade that has made no progress (under +0.5%) after 24 hours is closed instead of waiting for its stop

pace.what: Fluid pace: several trades a day when the evidence is there (learned from its own opportunity rate), Grade S always allowed

kelly.what: Edge-proportional sizing: fractional Kelly from the calibrated odds (bigger only when the edge is proven)

online-fast.what: Learns which evidence is right from every scored candidate, forgets old evidence fast (Kalman-style online learning)

online-slow.what: Same online learning, forgets slowly (more stable)

recal.what: Recalibrated odds: the raw odds are corrected by what really happened to past candidates at each odds level (learned from the live ledger; no correction until 20 separate market moves are scored)

tiers.what: Conviction tiers: a small probe (0.5% risk) when the edge is thin, standard (1-2%) with 3+ points of edge and 2 witnesses, high conviction (3-4%) with 8+ points, 3 witnesses and the market state on its side

bold.what: Bold: the same trades as the Arbiter at double the risk (8% of the account at the stop for Grade A, 4% for Grade B)

bestofday.what: Best case of the day: the bar eases gradually through the day (to half its safety margin by the last hour) when nothing better has appeared

weekpace.what: Weekly pace with carry-over: a quiet day's unused trade can be used later in the same week (up to 3 in one day)

bocpd-gate.what: Changepoint fast-track: Bayesian online changepoint detection on Bitcoin's return and market breadth; when a change is detected and the long side's graded calls since then beat their break-even over 15+ calls, longs unlock at once instead of waiting for the slow exam window

pairs.what: Pair trades: long the coin it likes most, short the one it dislikes most, among coins that move together (the market's swings cancel; tight stop even in wild markets)
